# Gelabber v0.8.0

Draft, collected while the `v0.8` line is developed. Feature PRs add their
entries here; the version PR completes the summary.

## Calls

- **Limits for the media WebSocket** (#286). Each client address may hold 16
  `/media/ws` sockets that have not joined a call yet (`MEDIA_PENDING_PER_IP`),
  the SFU 1024 in total (`MEDIA_PENDING_MAX`); past either cap the upgrade is
  answered `429` or `503`. A joined socket is pinged every 20 s
  (`MEDIA_HEARTBEAT_MS`) and leaves the call after 60 s without any answer
  (`MEDIA_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so a peer whose connection died without a close
  no longer stays in the room. The app rejoins on its own once the connection
  is back.
- **The old Go Live is gone** (#353). A screen share is the only Live: anyone
  with the Go Live permission can share a screen (with its sound), and several
  people can be live in the same call. The single per-channel Live claim, its
  `l`/`la` tracks, the `lc` nonce and the watch-only join were removed from the
  API, the media gateway and the app.

## GIFs

- **Faster GIF search, fewer KLIPY requests** (#350). Search and trending
  pages are kept in Redis for 10 minutes and shared by all users
  (`KLIPY_CACHE_SECS`, `0` turns it off), so a repeated search answers at
  once and costs no request from the key's quota. When KLIPY answers 429 the
  API stops asking it for the `Retry-After` (60 s by default) and the picker
  says the server's GIF quota is used up and when to try again, instead of
  loading. `/metrics` adds `gelabber_upstream_request_duration_seconds` for
  KLIPY's response times and `gelabber_cache_total` for cache hits. KLIPY
  testing keys allow only 100 requests per hour for the whole instance; see
  "GIFs" in `deploy/README.md`.

## Chat

- **Link previews say why a link got no card** (#349). The API log has one
  `info` line per link without a card, with its host and a reason
  (`refused`, `dns`, `timeout`, `status`, `content_type`, `no_metadata`, …),
  and `/metrics` counts them in `gelabber_link_previews_total` and
  `gelabber_link_preview_images_total`. A card whose image cannot be stored
  keeps its text. TikTok links get a card with title and image: the preview
  agent now ends in `like Twitterbot`. Hosts that resolve to a LAN address
  still get no card, on purpose; see "Link previews" in `deploy/README.md`.

## Upgrade notes

- **Clients older than v0.8 lose Go Live** (#353). Their Go Live button now
  fails: the server answers the old `l`/`la` track and the watch-only join with
  `bad_request`. Voice, camera and screen sharing keep working. Update the
  desktop app and reload the web app to go live again. Old `gb:live:*` keys in
  Redis expire on their own.
- **Own Caddy in front (homelab overlay):** add
  `header_up X-Forwarded-For {client_ip}` to the media upstream, as in
  `deploy/compose/Caddyfile.homelab`, and reload Caddy. The bundled Caddy
  gets it with the new `Caddyfile` (recreate the `proxy` container, see
  "Rollout and rollback with exact digests" in `deploy/README.md`). Media
  counts its pending-socket cap by the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry. Without the line, clients behind a
  CDN or tunnel your Caddy trusts all count as that proxy and share its 16
  slots, so after a server restart many reconnects get `429` and are retried.
  A proxy other than Caddy must send the client address in
  `X-Forwarded-For` (Nginx: `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`). Media logs a
  warning when its cap refuses a private address that sent no such header.
- **Keep `GELABBER_MEDIA_BIND` on loopback** (homelab overlay): like the API,
  media believes `X-Forwarded-For` from whoever reaches its port.
